description: The mathematics of how robots move: rigid body motion and coordinate frames, forward and inverse kinematics of serial manipulators, velocity kinematics and the Jacobian, Lagrangian and Newton-Euler dynamics, trajectory planning and the kinematics of wheeled mobile robots. Taught with interactive browser simulations of arms and mobile robots in which every formula is implemented and tested, applied to tasks such as fruit-picking arms and warehouse or farm delivery robots.
modelledOn: Lynch and Park, Modern Robotics: Mechanics, Planning, and Control
Craig, Introduction to Robotics: Mechanics and Control
Spong, Hutchinson and Vidyasagar, Robot Modeling and Control
Siciliano, Sciavicco, Villani and Oriolo, Robotics: Modelling, Planning and Control
outcomes: Represent the position and orientation of rigid bodies with rotation matrices, Euler angles, quaternions and homogeneous transformations.
Derive the forward kinematics of serial manipulators with Denavit-Hartenberg parameters and the product of exponentials formula.
Solve inverse kinematics analytically and numerically and reason about multiple solutions, workspace and reachability.
Compute the manipulator Jacobian, identify singularities and use the Jacobian for velocity control and static force analysis.
Derive equations of motion for manipulators with Lagrangian and Newton-Euler methods and use them for simulation and computed-torque control.
Plan smooth joint-space and task-space trajectories and model, simulate and steer differential-drive and other wheeled mobile robots.

units.title: Rigid body motion and coordinate frames
topics: Robots, links, joints and degrees of freedom; Grubler's formula; configuration space and task space
Rotation matrices and the special orthogonal group; composing rotations in fixed and moving frames
Representations of orientation: Euler angles, roll-pitch-yaw, axis-angle, unit quaternions; gimbal lock
Homogeneous transformations and the special Euclidean group; chaining frames
Twists, screws and the exponential map in outline; angular velocity and skew-symmetric matrices
Visualising frames and transformations in a browser simulation

units.title: Forward kinematics
topics: Serial chains: revolute and prismatic joints, link lengths and offsets
Denavit-Hartenberg convention, standard and modified; assigning frames step by step
The product of exponentials formula as an alternative to DH parameters
Forward kinematics of planar two- and three-link arms, SCARA and a six-axis industrial arm
Workspace: reachable and dexterous workspace; plotting it by sampling joint space

units.title: Inverse kinematics
topics: The inverse problem: existence, multiple solutions, elbow-up and elbow-down configurations
Analytical solutions for planar arms and the spherical wrist by kinematic decoupling
Numerical inverse kinematics: Newton-Raphson, Jacobian transpose and damped least squares
Joint limits, redundancy and choosing among solutions
Inverse kinematics for a fruit-picking or sorting arm reaching targets detected by a camera

units.title: Velocity kinematics and the Jacobian
topics: Linear and angular velocity of the end effector; the geometric and analytical Jacobian
Computing the Jacobian column by column; the space and body Jacobians
Singularities: boundary and interior singularities, loss of mobility, manipulability ellipsoids
Resolved-rate motion control and the pseudo-inverse for redundant arms
Statics: the Jacobian transpose relating end-effector forces to joint torques

units.title: Dynamics of manipulators
topics: Mass properties: centre of mass, inertia tensors, the parallel axis theorem
Lagrangian dynamics: kinetic and potential energy, the Euler-Lagrange equations for a two-link arm
Recursive Newton-Euler formulation and its computational efficiency
The manipulator equation: mass matrix, Coriolis and centrifugal terms, gravity; properties used in control
Forward dynamics for simulation; numerical integration and its stability
Joint-space control: PD with gravity compensation and computed-torque control; actuator and friction models

units.title: Trajectory planning
topics: Paths versus trajectories; time scaling
Point-to-point motion with cubic and quintic polynomials; trapezoidal velocity profiles
Via points and spline interpolation; blending segments
Task-space straight-line and circular paths; interpolating orientations with quaternion slerp
Time-optimal trajectories under velocity, acceleration and torque limits in outline

units.title: Kinematics of mobile robots
topics: Wheel types and constraints; holonomic and non-holonomic systems
Differential-drive kinematics: instantaneous centre of rotation, forward and inverse kinematics
Car-like, tricycle and omnidirectional (mecanum) platforms
Odometry from wheel encoders, error growth and dead reckoning
Path following: pure pursuit and simple feedback controllers for go-to-goal behaviour
Mobile robots in African settings: farm robots between crop rows and delivery robots on campus paths
Project: a simulated arm or mobile robot that completes a pick-and-place or delivery task
